title: Slain OPP officer committed no crime in Manitoulin shootout: SIU
subtitle: The man he shot and killed - Gary Brohman - was hiding a substaintial marijuana crop, investigation shows
article: The OPP officer fatally ambushed on Manitoulin Island last November has been cleared of criminal wrongdoing by the province's police watchdog.

On Friday, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit released their report on the Nov. 19, 2020, shootout that resulted in the deaths of OPP Const. Marc Hovingh and Gary Brohman, 60, concluding the 28-year OPP veteran was within his legal rights retaliate with deadly force.
On Nov. 18, Hovingh was dispatched to a rural property near Gore Bay on a trespassing complaint.
Brohman, the report states, had bulldozed a road through private property to a trailer he'd towed onto the site - all without permission from the property owner.

Hovingh attended the property but found the trailer empty, so he returned the next day at 10 a.m. with a second officer, where the property owner offered Brohman - who claimed legal rights to the land - heavy equipment to help remove his trailer from the property the next day, to which Brohman agreed.
That concession was soon revoked when a substantial marijuana crop was discovered nearby.
Prying open the trailer door, both officers entered and demanded Brohman leave immediately.
Brohman surprised Hovingh with a pump-action shotgun and fired three times, striking the officer twice in the thigh.
Although seriously injured, Hovingh returned fire, fatally striking Brohman in the head and chest.
Hovingh then collapsed and waited 90 minutes to be rescued by the OPP Emergency Response Team.
Found unconscious but breathing, Hovingh later died in hospital.
While SIU Director Joseph Martino said the act of forcing their way into the trailer raises doubts on if the officers were legally placed, Brohman's actions made the matter a moot point.

"Be that as it may, Mr. Brohman was at no point entitled to use lethal force against the officers," Martino wrote. "Whatever the officers' status inside the trailer, they were entitled to defend themselves."
Martino also found no fault in the 90-minute delay in rescuing the grievously-injured Hovingh from the trailer, as nobody knew Brohman's condition.

"As far as they knew, he could easily have been lying in wait in the trailer still capable of inflicting grievous bodily harm or death," Martino concluded, adding there were also concerns Brohman had booby-trapped the property.
